summary: British-born film director Alfred Hitchcock, master of suspense, spent decades subjecting crew and friends to cruel pranks and his leading actresses to abuse, culminating in his obsessive control, harassment and alleged sexual assault of Tippi Hedren in Hollywood in the early 1960s.

long run of cruel pranks on assistants, crew and friends during British career
crewman chained overnight and dosed with laxatives on a bet
his wish to mould a controllable actress and quotes about tormenting women
rough treatment of Madeleine Carroll and Janet Leigh on set

Hedren's 2017 statement after Weinstein; blackballing and his decline

notes: misogyny-manosphere is used for Hitchcock's personal hostility toward women, which the theme (organized misogyny) does not quite fit; no theme exists for workplace abuse by a boss, so labor-exploitation stands in for the crew pranks. main_span runs from his entry into film (1920) to Marnie (1964), after which the story treats his career as broken. Hedren's later statements set reaches_present. Guest spelled Geith in the description; Gheith is the usual spelling.
